posts.content:
What does it take to architect and secure an 11,000-satellite orbital mesh against state-sponsored Electronic Warfare, optical laser intercepts, and silicon-level fault injection?

Over the past few weeks, I used advanced multi-agent AI orchestration to engineer a 16-chapter technical monograph and built StarSec (CSF v1.0)—an open-source cybersecurity standard and astrodynamics evaluation suite for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) mega-constellations.

Most legacy space communications standards (like CCSDS) were conceived for Geostationary (GEO) satellites and bent-pipe relays—not relativistic 100 Gbps free-space optical meshes dynamically orbiting at 7.6 km/s.

Here is what StarSec introduces:

1️⃣ Spacecraft Hardware Hardening (RFC-002):
Hardware voltage glitching countermeasures inspired by real-world User Terminal exploits (Black Hat 2022). Includes sub-10ns crowbar zeroization, SRAM-PUF fuzzy extractors, and Dual-Core Lockstep (DCLS) monitors in C.

2️⃣ Capon MVDR Spatial Null-Steering (RFC-003):
Simulated 1,280-element Ku-band AESA phased array beamforming. Synthesizes a >150 dB cancellation null against high-power terrestrial chirp jammers under dynamic ±325 kHz Doppler shifts.

3️⃣ Sovereign Byzantine Quorum for TT&C (RFC-004):
Shamir (t, n) threshold secret sharing preventing single-point unauthorized telecommand execution or rogue de-orbit commands.

4️⃣ In-Orbit eBPF/XDP Line-Rate Filtering:
A verified static in-kernel eBPF packet filter dropping unauthenticated orbital frames in <1 µs with zero userspace overhead.

🔬 100% Reproducible & Zero-Cost:
The entire repository is accompanied by 7 deep R&D whitepapers, interactive Jupyter notebooks, and a local test runner where all 23 unit tests and C drivers compile and pass in under 10 seconds with zero cloud dependencies.

This project represents the sheer power of modern multi-agent AI engineering orchestration—bridging astrodynamics, RF electromagnetics, and post-quantum cryptography as a solo researcher.

Starlink has transformed global connectivity and space logistics. StarSec is an open-source tribute and research foundation dedicated to hardening the next generation of mega-constellations.

Feedback, architectural review, and critique from aerospace, satellite communications, and cybersecurity engineers are warmly invited!

Explore the open-source repository and whitepapers:

posts.content:
Hey everyone,

With Starlink scaling past 11,000 satellites and introducing V2 Mini/V3 spacecraft with optical laser crosslinks and Direct-to-Cell, satellite constellation security and resilience has become a critical engineering frontier.

I spent the last several weeks synthesizing open FCC/ITU filings, peer-reviewed AIAA/IEEE literature, and empirical telemetry to build a 16-chapter technical monograph and open-source cybersecurity standard: StarSec (CSF v1.0).

Key engineering areas covered:
- Astrodynamics: J2 secular nodal drift (-4.49 deg/day) and Foster collision probability (Pc).
- Phased Arrays: 1,280-element Ku AESA beamforming and Capon MVDR spatial null-steering (>150 dB cancellation).
- Hardware Security: Sub-10ns zeroization drivers, SRAM-PUF, and DCLS monitors inspired by terminal voltage-glitching exploits.
- In-Orbit Networking: Line-rate eBPF/XDP packet filtering and PQC ML-KEM-1024 laser ISL auth.

All code and simulations are open-source and run locally in <10s.

GitHub: https://github.com/techdeveloper-org/starlink-research-report
